summary: Destructive wiper executes on require and via exported sorgu() API
details: osinthell@1.0.5 is a destructive wiper targeting Windows hosts. index.js unconditionally requires seven sibling modules under./public/core/ that each run an IIFE at load time, so simply `require('osinthell')` triggers the payload with no further action. The payload (patlat) forcibly terminates critical Windows processes (explorer.exe, dwm.exe, csrss.exe, winlogon.exe) via execSync('taskkill /F /IM...'), recursively deletes C:\Windows, C:\Program Files, and C:\Windows\System32 via fs.rmSync with {recursive:true,force:true}, overwrites the system hosts file, zeroes the first 512 bytes of \\.\PhysicalDrive0 (the MBR) via fs.openSync/fs.writeSync, fork-bombs the host through detached self-spawning, exhausts memory, and issues execSync('shutdown /r /f /t 0'). index.js runs the same payload when executed directly, and the sole public export, module.exports.sorgu(userId), calls patlat() before process.exit(), so any consumer calling the advertised API also destroys the host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
